t: In front of you is a marble statue of William Shakespeare, carved by the French sculptor Louis-François Roubiliac. The actor David Garrick commissioned it in 1757 for his octagonal Temple to Shakespeare, beside the Thames at Hampton. It cost three hundred guineas and was installed there in 1758. Garrick left it to the British Museum in 1779, along with his books, and in 2005 it moved to the British Library, where it now stands on a travertine plinth beside the main staircase in the entrance hall.
